summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and severe sclerodermatous graft-versus-host disease was admitted for acute shortness of breath. Evaluation revealed no pulmonary embolism, but chest imaging showed worsening ground-glass opacities and new pleural effusions, consistent with hospital-acquired pneumonia or GVHD flare. He was treated with intravenous vancomycin and cefepime for eight days, with clinical improvement. Anemia worsened during admission, likely due to ruxolitinib, and he received one unit of red blood cells with symptomatic relief. Transaminitis developed, prompting reduction of ruxolitinib and sirolimus doses. Heart failure was managed with initiation of torsemide. Hypothyroidism was adjusted due to suppressed TSH, and palliative care recommended morphine for breathlessness. He was discharged home on optimized immunosuppressive, cardiac, and symptom management regimens with follow-up across multiple specialties.
